html:
The fifth caliph of the Abbasid caliphate, who ruled from 786 to 809, when its capital Baghdad was at the height of its wealth and fame.

For most of his reign the government was run by the Barmakids, a Persian family of viziers, until he suddenly turned on them and destroyed them in 803. His court drew poets, musicians, scholars and lawyers, and the work of translating and collecting knowledge that led to the House of Wisdom grew under him and his son al-Ma'mun. He fought the Byzantine Empire and forced it to pay tribute. He also exchanged embassies with Charlemagne and sent him an elephant.

He split the succession between two sons, al-Amin and al-Ma'mun, which led to civil war soon after he died at Tus in 809. Later storytellers made him the wise, wandering caliph of the One Thousand and One Nights, and that legend is how most people know him today.
sum: The fifth caliph of the Abbasid caliphate, who ruled from 786 to 809, when its capital Baghdad was at the height of its wealth and fame.
